label: Adjetivo (-al)
sentence: Learning a second language is not just useful for travelling; many studies show it also brings important ___ benefits for memory and concentration.
explanation: ADDITION → additional. Delante del sustantivo 'benefits' va un adjetivo; -al convierte sustantivos en adjetivos.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: The course covers grammar and vocabulary in detail; ___, every student receives one hour of individual pronunciation practice each week.
explanation: ADDITION → additionally. Conector al principio de la oración, separado por coma: adverbio.

label: Sustantivo (-ment)
sentence: After eight hours of difficult discussion the two sides finally reached an ___ that satisfied nobody completely but did end the strike.
explanation: AGREE → agreement. Después de 'an' va un sustantivo contable; -ment convierte verbos en sustantivos.

label: Prefijo negativo (dis-)
sentence: Although I respect your point of view and understand your reasons, I completely ___ with your opinion about banning cars from the city centre.
explanation: AGREE → disagree. 'Although' marca contraste: el sentido es negativo. Aquí falta un verbo, negado con dis-.

label: Sustantivo negativo (dis- + -ment)
sentence: A minor ___ about who should pay for the meal gradually turned into an argument that ruined the rest of the evening.
explanation: AGREE → disagreement. Sustantivo, y el contexto ('turned into an argument') pide el negativo: dis-.

label: Sustantivo (-ance)
sentence: ___ at the evening lectures has fallen so sharply this term that the university is seriously thinking of cancelling them altogether.
explanation: ATTEND → attendance. Es el sujeto de 'has fallen', así que necesitás un sustantivo.

label: Sustantivo de persona (-or)
sentence: Before the plane took off, a flight ___ walked down the aisle checking that every passenger had fastened their seatbelt correctly.
explanation: ATTEND → attendant. No todos los sustantivos de persona usan -er: attendant, assistant, applicant usan -ant.

label: Sustantivo (-tion)
sentence: The teacher asked the whole class to pay close ___ to the diagram on the board, because something very similar would appear in the exam.
explanation: ATTEND → attention. 'Pay ___' es una colocación fija con sustantivo.

label: Adjetivo (-able)
sentence: The afternoon heat was just about ___ as long as you stayed in the shade and drank plenty of water every hour.
explanation: BEAR → bearable. 'Just about ___' pide un adjetivo; -able significa 'que se puede soportar'.

label: Doble cambio (un- + -able)
sentence: The heat in the city during August was almost ___, so most families escaped to the coast for the entire month.
explanation: BEAR → bearable → unbearable. ¡Prefijo Y sufijo a la vez! El nivel más alto del examen combina ambos.

label: Sustantivo (-hood)
sentence: She wrote a beautiful book of memories about her ___ in a small fishing village on the northern coast of Spain.
explanation: CHILD → childhood. 'Her ___ in a village' pide un sustantivo; -hood expresa etapa o condición (adulthood, neighbourhood).

label: Adjetivo (-ish)
sentence: Refusing to speak to a colleague for an entire week over something so small strikes me as frankly ___ behaviour.
explanation: CHILD → childish. Delante de 'behaviour' va un adjetivo; -ish acá tiene sentido despectivo: 'propio de un chico'.

label: Sustantivo (-ity)
sentence: What makes his lectures so popular among students is the ___ with which he explains ideas that other people manage to make sound impossible.
explanation: CLEAR → clarity. 'The ___ with which' pide un sustantivo abstracto; clear pierde la e y toma -ity.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: Please write your name and full address ___ at the top of the form, because we cannot process applications that we are unable to read.
explanation: CLEAR → clearly. Modifica al verbo 'write' (cómo escribir): adverbio.

label: Prefijo + adjetivo
sentence: The assembly instructions that came with the furniture were so ___ that we spent the whole afternoon trying to figure out which screw went where.
explanation: CLEAR → unclear. El contexto (pasaron la tarde intentando entenderlas) pide sentido negativo: un- + adjetivo.

label: Adjetivo (-able)
sentence: Despite being one of the cheapest hotels in the city centre, the room was surprisingly clean, quiet and ___, so we decided to stay an extra night.
explanation: COMFORT → comfortable. Va en una lista de adjetivos (clean, quiet and ___), así que debe ser otro adjetivo.

label: Adverbio (-ably)
sentence: The car seats five adults ___, which makes it an ideal choice for a family that travels long distances at weekends.
explanation: COMFORT → comfortably. Modifica al verbo 'seats' (cómo se sientan): adverbio. Ojo, -able pierde la e final.

label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
sentence: The seats on the overnight bus were so ___ that hardly anyone managed to sleep for more than a few minutes at a time.
explanation: COMFORTABLE → uncomfortable. 'So ___ that nadie durmió' pide el adjetivo en negativo: prefijo un-.

label: Sustantivo (-tion)
sentence: After years of delays and rising costs, the ___ of the new hospital was finally completed last month, and local residents celebrated the opening with a small ceremony.
explanation: CONSTRUCT → construction. Después de 'the' y antes de 'of' casi siempre va un sustantivo.

label: Adjetivo (-ive)
sentence: Rather than simply listing everything that was wrong with the report, she offered several ___ suggestions about how the team could improve it before the deadline.
explanation: CONSTRUCT → constructive. 'Several ___ suggestions': delante de un sustantivo va un adjetivo; -ive forma adjetivos a partir de verbos.

label: Verbo (prefijo re-)
sentence: Using old photographs and the original architect's drawings, the town council plans to ___ the bridge exactly as it looked before the flood destroyed it.
explanation: CONSTRUCT → reconstruct. Después de 'to' va un infinitivo; el prefijo re- significa 'volver a hacer'.

label: Sustantivo (-ion)
sentence: The teacher returned the essay covered in red ink, but every single ___ was explained clearly in a note in the margin.
explanation: CORRECT → correction. Sujeto de 'was explained': necesitás un sustantivo contable.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: To everyone's surprise, the youngest student in the class answered all of the examiner's questions ___ and finished the test twenty minutes early.
explanation: CORRECT → correctly. Modifica al verbo 'answered' (¿cómo respondió?), así que es un adverbio.

label: Prefijo negativo (in-)
sentence: The referee's decision was so obviously ___ that even supporters of the winning team complained about it after the match.
explanation: CORRECT → incorrect. El contexto (todos se quejaron) pide negación; correct usa in-, no un-.

label: Adjetivo (-ous)
sentence: It was an extremely ___ decision to speak out publicly about the problem when she knew perfectly well that it might cost her the job.
explanation: COURAGE → courageous. Delante del sustantivo 'decision' va un adjetivo; -ous es un sufijo adjetival frecuente.

label: Verbo (prefijo dis-)
sentence: The very high price of the tickets seems almost designed to ___ ordinary families from visiting the museum more than once a year.
explanation: COURAGE → discourage. Después de 'to' va un infinitivo; dis- invierte el sentido de encourage.

label: Verbo (en-)
sentence: The school has introduced a new reading programme designed to ___ young children to pick up a book instead of a tablet.
explanation: COURAGE → encourage. A veces el prefijo en- forma el verbo (enable, enrich, enlarge).

label: Sustantivo (en- + -ment)
sentence: With a little ___ from his history teacher, he finally entered the writing competition and ended up winning first prize.
explanation: COURAGE → encouragement. Después de 'a little' va un sustantivo incontable; en- + -ment.

label: Sustantivo (-ion)
sentence: The ___ of the national park took almost fifteen years of difficult negotiation between the government and the farmers who owned the land.
explanation: CREATE → creation. 'The ___ of' pide un sustantivo; -ion convierte verbos en sustantivos.

label: Adjetivo (-ive)
sentence: Everyone in the family says my sister is the most ___ of us all, because she paints, writes her own songs and even designs her own clothes.
explanation: CREATE → creative. 'The most ___' es un superlativo, así que necesitas un adjetivo.

label: Sustantivo (-ivity)
sentence: What impressed the judges most was not her technique but the sheer ___ she showed in choosing such an unusual subject for the painting.
explanation: CREATE → creativity. Después de 'the sheer' va un sustantivo abstracto incontable.

label: Adjetivo (-ous)
sentence: Experienced climbers always warn beginners that attempting the north face of the mountain without a guide is extremely ___, especially in winter conditions.
explanation: DANGER → dangerous. 'Extremely ___' pide un adjetivo; -ous convierte sustantivos en adjetivos.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: The lorry was travelling ___ close to the car in front, and the driver was later fined a substantial amount for it.
explanation: DANGER → dangerously. Modifica al adjetivo 'close', así que necesitás un adverbio.

label: Verbo (prefijo en-)
sentence: Environmental groups argue that the proposed road would ___ several rare species of bird that still nest in the forest.
explanation: DANGER → endanger. Después de 'would' va un infinitivo; el prefijo en- convierte sustantivos en verbos.

label: Verbo (-en)
sentence: The sky began to ___ long before the storm actually arrived, and the street lights came on almost two hours earlier than usual.
explanation: DARK → darken. Después de 'began to' va un infinitivo; el sufijo -en convierte adjetivos en verbos (dark → darken).

label: Sustantivo (-ness)
sentence: As soon as the storm knocked out the electricity, the ___ of the house made it impossible to find the candles we kept in the kitchen drawer.
explanation: DARK → darkness. 'The ___ of the house' pide un sustantivo; los adjetivos forman sustantivos con -ness.

label: Sustantivo (-ence)
sentence: Even after living in both countries for several years, she still finds it fascinating how big the ___ between British and American English can be.
explanation: DIFFER → difference. 'How big the ___' pide un sustantivo; el verbo differ forma difference con -ence.

label: Adjetivo (-ent)
sentence: Although the two brothers grew up in the same house and went to the same school, they have completely ___ opinions about almost every subject.
explanation: DIFFER → different. Delante del sustantivo 'opinions' va un adjetivo.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: If I could start the whole project again, I would organise the first few weeks quite ___ and ask for help much earlier than I did.
explanation: DIFFER → differently. Modifica al verbo 'organise', o sea adverbio.

label: Adjetivo (-al)
sentence: Before you plug in the heater, make sure that a qualified expert has checked all the ___ connections at the back of the unit.
explanation: ELECTRIC → electrical. Delante de 'connections' va un adjetivo; -al se usa para 'relativo a la electricidad'.

label: Sustantivo de persona (-ian)
sentence: You should take the car to a qualified ___ instead of trying to repair the engine yourself with videos from the internet.
explanation: ELECTRIC → electrician. -ian forma profesiones (musician, politician, technician).

label: Sustantivo (-ity)
sentence: The storm cut off the ___ to the whole village, and it took engineers almost two days to repair the cables that had come down.
explanation: ELECTRIC → electricity. Después de 'the' va un sustantivo; -ity forma sustantivos abstractos.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: The children ran ___ towards the beach the moment the car doors opened, leaving their parents to carry all the bags by themselves.
explanation: EXCITE → excitedly. Modifica al verbo 'ran' (cómo corrieron), así que necesitás un adverbio.

label: Sustantivo (-ment)
sentence: When the results were announced, her ___ was so obvious that everyone in the room could see she had been dreaming about this moment for years.
explanation: EXCITE → excitement. 'Her ___ was' necesita un sustantivo; -ment convierte verbos en sustantivos.

label: Adjetivo (-ing)
sentence: Everyone agreed it was the most ___ match of the whole season, with three goals scored in the final ten minutes of the game.
explanation: EXCITE → exciting. Describe la COSA que provoca la emoción (el partido), no a quien la siente: por eso -ing y no -ed.

label: Adjetivo (-ed)
sentence: The audience sat completely ___ as the magician calmly explained exactly how the trick they had just watched had been done.
explanation: FASCINATE → fascinated. Describe cómo SE SIENTE el público, no cómo es: por eso -ed y no -ing.

label: Adjetivo (-ing / -ed)
sentence: The documentary about deep-sea creatures was absolutely ___, and we ended up watching the whole series in a single weekend.
explanation: FASCINATE → fascinating. -ing describe la cosa que causa la sensación; -ed describe a quien la siente (I was fascinated).

label: Sustantivo (-ion)
sentence: His lifelong ___ with insects began when he found a rare beetle in the garden at the age of six and kept it in a jar.
explanation: FASCINATE → fascination. 'His lifelong ___' pide un sustantivo abstracto.

label: Adjetivo (-ate)
sentence: We were ___ enough to get the last two tickets, although we ended up sitting at opposite ends of the theatre.
explanation: FORTUNE → fortunate. 'Were ___ enough to' pide un adjetivo.

label: Adverbio (doble cambio)
sentence: The fire spread through the building in a matter of minutes, but ___, all the employees had already left for lunch and nobody was hurt.
explanation: FORTUNE → fortunate → fortunately. ¡Doble transformación! Sustantivo → adjetivo → adverbio. Muy típico del examen.

label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
sentence: It was extremely ___ that the concert was cancelled on the very day her parents had travelled two hundred miles to hear her play.
explanation: FORTUNATE → unfortunate. El sentido de la frase (se canceló justo ese día) es negativo: prefijo un-.

label: Adjetivo (-ly)
sentence: The staff at the little hotel were so ___ that we felt completely at home within an hour of arriving, even though nobody spoke our language.
explanation: FRIEND → friendly. Después de 'were so' va un adjetivo. Ojo: -ly acá forma ADJETIVO, no adverbio.

label: Sustantivo (-ship)
sentence: Their ___ began at primary school more than thirty years ago, and they still meet for coffee every single Saturday morning.
explanation: FRIEND → friendship. 'Their ___ began' pide un sustantivo abstracto; -ship expresa relación o estado.

label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
sentence: I found the atmosphere in the office rather ___ during my first week, though I later realised that everyone was simply under enormous pressure.
explanation: FRIENDLY → unfriendly. 'Rather ___' pide un adjetivo y el contraste con 'though' marca sentido negativo.

label: Adjetivo (-ing)
sentence: There is a ___ number of people in the city who have decided to give up their cars altogether and travel everywhere by bicycle instead.
explanation: GROW → growing. 'A ___ number' pide un adjetivo delante del sustantivo.

label: Sustantivo irregular
sentence: Scientists say that the recent ___ in average temperatures is one of the clearest signs of climate change affecting the region.
explanation: GROW → growth. Sustantivo irregular con -th, como wide → width o strong → strength.

label: Adverbio (-ily)
sentence: ___, the missing documents turned up in a drawer just hours before the meeting, so the presentation could go ahead as planned.
explanation: HAPPY → happily. Los adjetivos en -y cambian a -ily (easy → easily, angry → angrily).

label: Sustantivo (-ness)
sentence: Money certainly makes daily life easier, but most researchers now agree that it has surprisingly little effect on long-term ___.
explanation: HAPPY → happiness. Después de 'long-term' va un sustantivo; -ness convierte adjetivos en sustantivos abstractos.

label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
sentence: She was so ___ in her first job that she resigned after only four months and went travelling around South America instead.
explanation: HAPPY → unhappy. Renunció a los cuatro meses: el sentido es negativo, prefijo un-.

label: Adjetivo (-ful)
sentence: The advice you gave me before the interview turned out to be incredibly ___, and I honestly don't think I would have got the job without it.
explanation: HELP → helpful. Después de 'incredibly' (adverbio) y el verbo 'be' va un adjetivo; -ful = 'lleno de'.

label: Adjetivo (-less)
sentence: Watching the flood slowly destroy everything they had built over twenty years, the family felt completely ___ and could do nothing but wait.
explanation: HELP → helpless. Después de 'felt' va un adjetivo; -less significa 'sin', o sea sin capacidad de ayudar.

label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
sentence: The instructions that came with the furniture were so ___ that in the end we assembled the whole thing by guessing where each piece went.
explanation: HELPFUL → unhelpful. El resultado ('lo armamos adivinando') marca sentido negativo: prefijo un-.

label: Prefijo negativo (dis-)
sentence: It would be ___ of me to pretend that I had read the entire report when in fact I only glanced at the summary.
explanation: HONEST → dishonest. 'Pretender que leí todo cuando no' es negativo; con honest el prefijo es dis-, no un-.

label: Adverbio (doble cambio)
sentence: The new manager speaks to every member of staff ___, which is probably why the whole team trusts her decisions so much.
explanation: HONEST → honestly. Describe cómo habla (verbo 'speaks'), así que es un adverbio de modo.

label: Sustantivo (-y)
sentence: What I admire most about him is his complete ___, even when telling the truth is clearly going to cost him something important.
explanation: HONEST → honesty. Después de 'his complete' va un sustantivo abstracto.

label: Sustantivo (-ism)
sentence: After three years of studying ___ at university and writing for the student magazine, she was offered a job at a small local newspaper.
explanation: JOURNAL → journalism. Después de 'studying' va un sustantivo; -ism nombra la profesión o disciplina.

label: Sustantivo de persona (-ist)
sentence: The newspaper sent its most experienced ___ to cover the elections, since she had been reporting on politics for two decades.
explanation: JOURNAL → journalist. -ist forma la persona que ejerce una actividad (artist, scientist, pianist).

label: Prefijo negativo (il-)
sentence: Parking on the pavement is completely ___ in this neighbourhood, and the police give out dozens of fines every single week.
explanation: LEGAL → illegal. Ante l, el prefijo negativo es il- (illogical, illegible).

label: Adverbio negativo (il- + -ly)
sentence: The van had been parked ___ across the entrance for so many days that the council eventually had it towed away.
explanation: LEGAL → illegally. Adverbio (modifica a 'parked') y el contexto pide el negativo: il- delante de l.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: In this country you are ___ required to carry some form of photographic identification whenever you are driving a vehicle.
explanation: LEGAL → legally. Modifica al participio 'required': hace falta un adverbio.

label: Sustantivo (-hood)
sentence: Given how much rain has already fallen this week, there is every ___ that Saturday's match will be postponed once again.
explanation: LIKELY → likelihood. 'There is every ___ that' pide un sustantivo; -hood forma sustantivos abstractos.

label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
sentence: Given the amount of traffic on the motorway at this time of day, it seems highly ___ that they will arrive in time for the beginning of the ceremony.
explanation: LIKELY → unlikely. El contexto (mucho tráfico) indica sentido negativo: necesitas el prefijo un-. Sigue siendo adjetivo.

label: Sustantivo irregular
sentence: The doctor asked him to describe the exact ___ of the pain so she could decide which tests were necessary.
explanation: LOCATE → location. La -e final se elimina antes de añadir -ion.

label: Verbo (prefijo re-)
sentence: When the company announced that it would ___ its head office to another country, almost half the staff decided to look for new jobs.
explanation: LOCATE → relocate. Después de 'would' va un infinitivo sin to; re- indica cambio de lugar.

label: Sustantivo (-ance)
sentence: The final ___ of the school orchestra was so impressive that the audience stood up and applauded for almost five minutes.
explanation: PERFORM → performance. 'The final ___ of' pide un sustantivo; perform forma performance con -ance.

label: Persona (-er)
sentence: As a young ___, she used to get so nervous before going on stage that she could hardly remember the first line of the song.
explanation: PERFORM → performer. 'A young ___' pide un sustantivo de persona; -er indica quien hace la acción.

label: Adjetivo (-ible)
sentence: Under the new parking rules it is no longer ___ to leave your car along this street between eight in the morning and six in the evening.
explanation: PERMIT → permissible. 'It is no longer ___ to...' pide un adjetivo; -ible se usa para 'que se puede'.

label: Sustantivo irregular (-ssion)
sentence: Visitors must obtain written ___ from the head office before they are allowed to take photographs anywhere inside the museum.
explanation: PERMIT → permission. Cambio irregular: -ssion, no -tion. Igual que admit → admission.

label: Sustantivo de persona (-er)
sentence: My uncle worked as a professional ___ for over twenty years, travelling around the world to capture images of wildlife for nature magazines.
explanation: PHOTOGRAPH → photographer. 'Worked as a ___' pide un sustantivo de persona; se forman con -er/-or/-ist.

label: Adjetivo (-ic)
sentence: The museum has an extraordinary ___ collection covering more than a century of everyday life in the city and its surrounding villages.
explanation: PHOTOGRAPH → photographic. Delante del sustantivo 'collection' va un adjetivo; -ic es un sufijo adjetival muy común.

label: Sustantivo (-y)
sentence: He became seriously interested in ___ at the age of twelve, when his grandfather gave him an old camera that somehow still worked perfectly.
explanation: PHOTOGRAPH → photography. Después de la preposición 'in' va un sustantivo; -y nombra la disciplina.

label: Prefijo negativo (im-)
sentence: The manager insisted that finishing such a complex project in a single week was completely ___ and asked the client for at least one more month.
explanation: POSSIBLE → impossible. El contexto pide negación, y ante p se usa im-, no un- (impatient, impolite).

label: Sustantivo (-ity)
sentence: Although the weather forecast looks good for the weekend, there is still a strong ___ that the outdoor concert will be moved to the indoor arena.
explanation: POSSIBLE → possibility. 'A strong ___' pide un sustantivo; los adjetivos en -ble cambian a -bility.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: She promised she would help us with the move if she ___ could, but she has already agreed to work at the hospital that weekend.
explanation: POSSIBLE → possibly. 'If she ___ could' modifica al verbo: hace falta un adverbio.

label: Prefijo negativo (ir-)
sentence: Leaving a campfire burning in the middle of a dry forest is one of the most ___ things a visitor can possibly do.
explanation: RESPONSIBLE → irresponsible. Ante r, el prefijo negativo es ir- (irregular, irrelevant).

label: Sustantivo (-ility)
sentence: Taking ___ for a mistake in front of your colleagues is far more impressive than quietly pretending that it never happened.
explanation: RESPONSIBLE → responsibility. 'Taking ___ for' es una colocación fija con sustantivo.

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: The campaign encourages young drivers to behave ___ and to leave the car at home whenever they are planning to drink.
explanation: RESPONSIBLE → responsibly. Modifica al verbo 'behave': adverbio. Ojo, -ble pasa a -bly.

label: Verbo (-ize/-ise)
sentence: Before you hand in your essay, remember to ___ your main arguments in a short final paragraph so the reader remembers your key points.
explanation: SUMMARY → summarize/summarise. -ize (US) o -ise (UK) convierten sustantivos en verbos; Cambridge acepta ambas grafías.

label: Sustantivo (base)
sentence: Please write a short ___ of the article in no more than one hundred words and hand it in before Friday afternoon.
explanation: SUMMARIZE → summary. 'A short ___ of' pide un sustantivo. Acá la transformación va al revés: del verbo al sustantivo.

label: Prefijo (mis-) + pasado
sentence: I'm so sorry about the confusion yesterday; I completely ___ your instructions and sent the report to the wrong department.
explanation: UNDERSTAND → misunderstood. mis- = hacer algo mal, y el contexto (yesterday) exige pasado: misunderstood. Es un verbo.

label: Adjetivo (-able)
sentence: It is perfectly ___ that you feel nervous before an interview; almost everybody does, including the people who are interviewing you.
explanation: UNDERSTAND → understandable. 'It is perfectly ___ that...' pide un adjetivo; -able significa 'que se puede'.

label: Sustantivo (-ing)
sentence: Living abroad for a year gave her a far deeper ___ of how differently two people can see exactly the same problem.
explanation: UNDERSTAND → understanding. 'A far deeper ___ of' pide un sustantivo.

label: Adjetivo (-ful)
sentence: The old paper map turned out to be surprisingly ___ once we left the main road and started exploring the tiny villages up in the hills.
explanation: USE → useful. Después de 'to be surprisingly' va un adjetivo; -ful significa 'lleno de'.

label: Adjetivo (-less)
sentence: After arguing with him for more than an hour, I realised that trying to change his mind was completely ___, so I simply gave up and left.
explanation: USE → useless. El contexto (gave up) indica sentido negativo: -less = 'sin'. Es lo contrario de useful.

label: Persona (-er)
sentence: Every ___ has to create a password of at least ten characters before the system will allow them to log in for the first time.
explanation: USE → user. 'Every ___' pide un sustantivo contable de persona; -er indica quien hace la acción.

label: Prefijo negativo (in-)
sentence: The stain was almost ___ in ordinary daylight, but under the lamp you could see exactly where the coffee had been spilt.
explanation: VISIBLE → invisible. El contraste con 'but under the lamp you could see' marca sentido negativo: prefijo in-.

label: Sustantivo (-ility)
sentence: Thick fog reduced ___ to less than fifty metres, and as a result the motorway was closed for most of the morning.
explanation: VISION → visibility. Objeto directo de 'reduced': hace falta un sustantivo.

label: Adjetivo (-ible)
sentence: The instructions on the medicine bottle were printed in letters so small that they were barely ___ without a magnifying glass.
explanation: VISION → visible. Ojo: no es 'visionable'. Algunos adjetivos usan -ible y cambian la raíz (vision → visible).

label: Adverbio (-ly)
sentence: The novel has been ___ translated since it first appeared and is now available in more than thirty different languages.
explanation: WIDE → widely. Modifica al participio 'translated': adverbio.

label: Verbo (-en)
sentence: The city council has announced ambitious plans to ___ the main road next year in order to reduce the terrible traffic jams during rush hour.
explanation: WIDE → widen. Después de 'to' va un verbo; -en convierte adjetivos en verbos (strengthen, shorten, brighten).

label: Sustantivo (irregular)
sentence: Before ordering the carpet, measure both the length and the ___ of the room and write both figures down somewhere safe.
explanation: WIDE → width. Después de 'the' va un sustantivo. Es irregular: cambia la vocal y toma -th, como long → length.

label: Adjetivo (-y)
sentence: We had planned a picnic by the lake, but the weather was so ___ that we could hardly keep the blanket on the ground.
explanation: WIND → windy. 'The weather was so ___' pide un adjetivo; muchos sustantivos de clima forman adjetivos con -y.
